scope: Saved gS/lPt/FJ functions in separate timeboxed VM contexts with synthetic memory providers; original client, storage and transport not exercised.
conclusions: gS blocks the chat write path for a truthy guard; otherwise a nonnull temporary value is written before the persisted target. An arbitrary supplied mode object is passed to both setter substitutes without enum validation.

lPt computes capability before its extension/work-only decision. Both persisted-mode branches preserve an arbitrary object in these fixtures. Synchronous access getter failure can prevent a normal extension result.

Generic FJ undefined getter fallback skips coercion. Functional updates may coerce the old stored value and delay=0 selects the delayed publisher; direct values bypass coercion. Equal NaN skips publication while still writing the atom.

Synchronous first-write/publisher throw prevents the later operation in the selected functions. Returned rejected Promises are distinct: these functions do not await them, and the later operation still runs in the fixture. The observer handles rejection independently to protect the runner.
limits: This explicitly authorized run executes only three saved complete tiny functions with memory substitutes, not an original client, UI, real provider, localStorage, filesystem persistence, native bridge or model task.
FJ optional coerce/delay fixtures describe the generic saved factory only. The actual MODE Fu two-argument use is inherited and these fixtures do not establish those options for it.

Memory publishers intentionally leave the persisted Map unchanged. Calls to publisher/atom substitutes prove only context-local control flow, not the real hI/ARt persistence chain, source dispatch, delivery, backend or durability.

Capability service behavior, function/property getters beyond these fixtures, real scheduling, cancellation, every dependency exception, all resolver inputs and end-to-end mode transitions are not covered.
The runner catches Promise rejection through an independent immediate observer; that handling is not attributed to the selected source functions.
The three source texts and runner/source snapshots remain ignored local-only; formal candidates contain pins and finite observation metadata, not source implementation text.
Old MODE26, Storage46, global journal, runtime ledger and public products were not edited. Simulation does not establish Codex ownership, real persistence or full analysis completion.
